name: Knowledge Tracing for Learning Path Recommendation (2023-2026 Survey)
venue: Representative venues include AAAI 2023 and 2026, KDD 2024, Knowledge-Based Systems 2024, Information Processing & Management 2026, Scientific Reports 2025, Electronics 2025, and Applied Soft Computing 2026.
category: Student Modeling; Knowledge Tracing; Personalized Learning Path Recommendation
problem_setting: Given a learner interaction history, target concepts, and a candidate set of learning objects or exercises, the system estimates the learner's evolving mastery state and recommends an ordered learning path that maximizes learning gain, improves efficiency, respects prerequisite or similarity relations, adapts item difficulty, and optionally revisits forgotten concepts.
core_method: The 2023-2026 line combines KT as a learner-state estimator or simulator with path generation. SRC (AAAI 2023) formulates full-path recommendation as set-to-sequence ranking, uses a concept-aware encoder and LSTM decoder, optimizes the policy by policy gradient, and adds a KT auxiliary predictor for stability. The 2024 process-type PLP method uses DKT to annotate historical learner states, process mining to generate flowchart-style paths with sequence, parallel, and selection gateways, and decision mining for branch recommendation. DLPR (KDD 2024) adds item-difficulty-aware hierarchical reinforcement learning over learning and practice items. LPReKL (Electronics 2025) combines masked multi-step DKT, Qwen2-32B prompt generation, BERT retrieval from an exercise bank, and a KT feedback loop to refine LLM-generated reference exercises. RL-DKT (Scientific Reports 2025) uses DKT states as the environment state for an RL task-selection agent. FKGRec (Information Processing & Management 2026) adds forgetting-factor and knowledge-graph-aware MemGNN prediction so RL can balance new and forgotten concepts. IFLPR (Applied Soft Computing 2026) introduces forgetting-curve and centrality-based prerequisite filtering plus cross-model supervision between cognitive diagnosis and KT to stabilize exercise difficulty matching. KnowLP (AAAI 2026) is complementary: it uses GraphRAG-induced prerequisite and similarity graphs for path planning, which can be combined with KT state estimation.
data_sources: ASSIST09/ASSISTments 2009-2010, Junyi Academy, Huawei industrial education logs, KDD Cup 2010, Cognitive Tutor, MOOCCubeX, MOOPer, XES3G5M, KES-Junyi, KES-ASSIST09, and simulator environments derived from trained KT models are repeatedly used across the representative works; exact dataset inclusion differs by paper [uncertain].
evaluation_metrics: Common metrics include learning effect or promotion score such as E_T/E_phi, goal promotion under a fixed path length, learning steps to reach target mastery, task completion time, dropout or engagement indicators, KT prediction metrics such as AUC/ACC/BCE, difficulty matching metrics such as Cog-Gap and Diff-MAD, and recommendation metrics such as Hit@K or NDCG@K in graph-style variants; exact metric sets differ by paper [uncertain].
baselines: Representative baselines include Random, rule-based path ordering, MPC with KT simulation, GRU4Rec, DQN, BKT, DKT, CoKT-based simulators, FISM, CluLSTM, LightGCN, GEHRL, SKarRec, KGNN-KT, KNN, Actor-Critic, contextual bandit, RLTutor, CSEAL, and graph/RL path planners; exact baseline coverage differs by paper [uncertain].
strengths: KT provides a compact and updateable mastery vector, making path recommendation more student-aware than static course graphs or pure collaborative filtering. It naturally supports cold-start diagnostics, weak-concept targeting, offline simulation before deployment, and real-time adaptation after each exercise. When combined with knowledge graphs, difficulty modeling, forgetting factors, and LLM retrieval, the approach can generate paths that are not only relevant but also pedagogically constrained, explainable, and aligned with long-term learning gain.
limitations: Most results remain offline and depend on KT-based simulators, which can create evaluator bias when the same or similar KT model is used for both recommendation and evaluation. Strong performance requires high-quality exercise-concept tags, sufficient learner interaction logs, reliable prerequisite graphs, and careful reward design. RL-based methods raise ethical and operational concerns if deployed without guardrails. LLM-enhanced methods improve semantic coverage but add latency, cost, hallucination risk, and prompt sensitivity. Cross-paper comparison is difficult because learning path definitions, datasets, candidate-set construction, and metrics are not standardized.
fit_for_current_project: High fit. The current course recommendation agent already has a Go backend, Vue frontend, Neo4j knowledge graph, learning-progress data, and DeepSeek integration. A practical transfer path is to add a KT service that outputs per-concept mastery, use Neo4j prerequisite and similarity relations to construct candidate concepts, rank candidate resources by expected mastery gain and difficulty match, and use the assistant module only for explanation or path narration rather than as the sole recommender. The approach is especially suitable for AI-course learning where concept prerequisites and weak-point remediation matter.
implementation_complexity: Medium-high. A conservative MVP can be implemented by training DKT/SAKT/AKT in a Python service, exposing mastery vectors to the Go recommend module, and ranking Neo4j-backed candidates with a simple expected-gain heuristic. Adding offline RL, forgetting-aware review scheduling, LLM-generated exercises, and full simulator-based evaluation is substantially more complex and should be staged after the KT plus graph-ranking baseline is stable.
paper_patent_value: High. For a CCF-B-style paper, the strongest angle is a closed-loop framework that combines KT-based mastery estimation, educational knowledge-graph constraints, difficulty and forgetting-aware path optimization, and LLM-generated explanations evaluated with reproducible offline simulators and ablations. For patent claims, valuable points include the KT-KG-LLM closed-loop recommendation pipeline, dynamic branch/path adjustment from mastery vectors, forgetting-aware action-space construction, and safety-controlled LLM retrieval from a verified exercise bank.
recommended_action: Build a staged prototype: first standardize concept IDs and exercise-to-concept mappings; then train or integrate a DKT/SAKT baseline and expose a mastery-vector API; next implement a graph-constrained path ranker in the recommend module with expected mastery gain, prerequisite readiness, difficulty smoothness, and review need as scoring terms; finally evaluate against Random, shortest-prerequisite-path, GRU4Rec-style sequential recommendation, and a simple DQN/RL baseline using ASSIST09 or project logs before adding DeepSeek-based explanations.
